chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated from the four men, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from al-Ala' ibn Razeen, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:
Expect the cry to come to you surprisingly from the direction of Damascus; in it is great deliverance for you.

key_terms.الصَّوْتَ: The cry or call (often referring to the call of the Mahdi or a specific sign)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the cry from Damascus in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), the 'sudden cry' (al-Sayha) from Damascus is interpreted by Shia scholars as a specific sign preceding the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi, often linked to the initial military or political shifts in the Levant. This event serves as a herald of divine intervention, marking the transition from the era of occultation to the establishment of global justice, thereby offering believers hope and spiritual readiness for the imminent relief (al-Faraj).

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (66) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from the previous four narrators from al-Hasan bin Mahboob from al-Ala’ bin Razeen from Muhammad bin Muslim that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:
“Expect the cry to come to you surprisingly from the direction of Damascus. Then great deliverance will come to you.”
